name: tado° Smart Radiator Thermostat X (EU)

radios.note: CSA lists Thread and Bluetooth transport interfaces. Bluetooth is presumably used for setup.

matter.note: CSA has several entries for this product (hardware VA04, firmware 1.0 in the snippets seen).

apple_home.note: Linked with a Matter code from the tado° app or the device QR code. Needs a Thread border router: Bridge X, another tado° X border router, or a third-party one.

google_home.note: tado° has a setup guide for Google Home over Matter. Needs a Thread border router.

alexa.note: Needs a Matter-capable Echo or eero plus a Thread border router (tado° names Bridge X, Heat Pump Optimizer X or Wireless Receiver X). tado° advises adding the device in its own app first to keep firmware updates.

smartthings.note: tado° names SmartThings among Matter platforms in a search snippet only. No tado° SmartThings setup guide was found.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's tado page says tado° X devices are not supported by the tado integration and must be used through the Matter integration.

hubRequired.note: tado° says the Bridge X or any other Thread border router connects it to the internet. The Bridge X is sold separately and does not work with older tado° V3+ devices.

localControl.note: No tado° page found that describes offline or local-only control of the valve over Matter.

systems.value: M30 × 1.5 valves; Danfoss RA, RAV, RAVL adapters included
systems.note: tado° says most owners can mount it without an adapter. Oventrop M30 × 1.0 valves need an adapter tado° does not supply.

power.note: tado° pages are described as saying it charges over USB-C about once a year (about 2 hours). This came from a search summary; capacity was not confirmed.

summary: The tado° Smart Radiator Thermostat X replaces the head on a radiator valve and talks Matter over Thread. It fits M30 × 1.5 mm valves directly, and tado° ships Danfoss RA, RAV and RAVL adapters in the box. Apple Home, Google Home and Alexa connect through Matter, and Home Assistant uses its Matter integration. It needs a Thread border router, typically tado°'s Bridge X.
caveats: Needs a Thread border router; tado° sells the Bridge X, which does not work with tado° V3+ devices.
Adding the valve to several Matter platforms can slightly shorten battery life, per tado°.
Oventrop M30 × 1.0 valves need an adapter that tado° does not provide.
